name: donna
description: Runs in parallel to your coding agent and assesses the system-wide impact of its change before you open a pull request: affected services, design conformance, backward compatibility, production risk, required tests, and reviewers.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No assessment yet.

Donna watches for changes your coding agent makes and assesses their system-wide impact before you open a PR.

[Assess Current Change](command:donna.assess)
[Open Scorecard](command:donna.openScorecard)
[Connect Integrations](command:donna.connectIntegrations)

No context pack configured? Point Donna at your service map, ADRs and ownership records:
[Create Config](command:donna.initConfig)

donna.contextPack.markdownDescription: Path to a directory holding `donna.json`, the ADRs, ownership records and test expectations. Leave empty to look for `donna.json` at the workspace root. Useful when the context pack is maintained separately from the code it describes.

donna.baseRef.markdownDescription: Git ref to compare against. Empty means the merge base with the default branch (`origin/main`, `main`, `origin/master`, `master`, in that order) — which is what you want, because comparing with the branch tip would attribute other people's commits to your change.

donna.watch.enabled.markdownDescription: Re-assess automatically when files change. This is what makes Donna run *in parallel* to a coding agent: it reacts to the agent's edits without you asking.

donna.watch.debounceMs.markdownDescription: Quiet period after the last file change before re-assessing. Coding agents write files in bursts; this waits for the burst to finish rather than assessing a half-written change.

donna.blastRadiusDepth.markdownDescription: How many import hops to follow when working out who depends on the changed modules. Beyond about 3 the answer in a large repo is "most of the codebase", which is true but not actionable — the scorecard reports when the traversal was cut short.

donna.llm.enabled.markdownDescription: Allow the model pass, which judges design intent written in prose that no mechanical rule can check. Deterministic checks always run regardless.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Only when you run `Donna: Assess With Model Pass`.
Automatically when the deterministic checks find a conflict or an unchecked constraint, so the model has something concrete to judge. Recommended.
On every settled change. Highest coverage, highest token spend.
Use the editor's Language Model API, reusing whatever subscription you are already signed in to in VS Code. No API key needed.
Call the Anthropic API directly with a key stored in VS Code's secret storage.

donna.llm.vscodeModel.markdownDescription: Preferred model `family` from the editor's Language Model API (for example `claude-sonnet-4.5`, `gpt-4o`). Empty picks the first available.

donna.llm.anthropicModel.description: Model ID used when the provider is "anthropic".

donna.llm.maxFilesPerReview.description: Cap on how many changed files are sent to the model in one pass.

donna.diagnostics.enabled.description: Also publish findings as squiggles in the Problems pane.

donna.diagnostics.floor.description: Least severe status that gets a squiggle. Everything still appears in the Donna views.

donna.demo.scenarioDir.markdownDescription: Directory of prepared demo scenarios, used by `Donna: Run Demo Scenario`. This stands in for a coding agent so the three-agent flow can be demonstrated end to end.
